title: Team and ops
hired_for: An owner hires this screen so the work gets done on time by the right people at the right cost, and the business keeps running when the founder or any one person is away.

jobs.job: Hold the warehouse to its promise to ship on time and right
jobs.why: Late or wrong orders bring tickets, refunds and lost repeat buyers. Most 3PL contracts set a ship time, but few brands check it every week.

watch.metric: share of orders shipped within the agreed time and mis-pick rate, weekly
watch.source: Shopify fulfilment timestamps and 3PL reports

drives.metric: where is my order tickets per 100 orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 84% of orders ship within 1 business day against a 98% promise. After: the gap is raised with the 3PL and on-time shipping is 97% within 3 weeks.

jobs.job: Get my time back from work others can do
jobs.why: When the founder runs every task, growth stops at the founder's hours. Moving routine work to a named owner frees time for the few decisions only the founder can make.

watch.metric: founder hours per week on routine tasks, self-logged in the brand brain (proxy: count of recurring tasks with the founder as owner)
watch.source: brand brain task and owner list

drives.metric: founder hours on growth work per week

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the founder owns 23 of 40 recurring tasks and spends 30 hours a week on them. After: 12 move to named owners and founder routine time falls to 15 hours within 2 months.

jobs.job: Staff support for what is coming
jobs.why: A sale, a launch or the holidays can triple tickets. Without the right cover, reply times climb and shoppers cancel or dispute.

watch.metric: first reply time in hours and open ticket backlog, daily
watch.source: Gorgias or Zendesk

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: first reply takes 19 hours and backlog is 640 tickets after a sale. After: a temp agent and new macros bring reply time to 4 hours within 10 days.

jobs.job: Run a weekly trading review on the numbers that matter
jobs.why: Without a fixed weekly look at sales, margin, stock and cash, problems surface late and decisions drift.

watch.metric: share of weeks with the trading review held and at least 1 decision logged
watch.source: decision log and meeting notes in the brand brain

drives.metric: time from a problem showing to a decision

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the review happens about 2 weeks in 5. After: it runs every week for 30 minutes and logs 3 decisions on average.

jobs.job: Check vendor and warehouse bills against the work done
jobs.why: 3PL and agency invoices often carry wrong rates, double charges or fees outside the contract. Nobody checks them against order counts.

watch.metric: invoice overcharge dollars found per month, 3PL and vendor invoices against Shopify order counts and the rate card
watch.source: 3PL and vendor invoices, Shopify orders, contracts in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the 3PL bill is paid as sent. After: a check against orders finds $1,800 a month in extra pick fees, credited from next month.

jobs.job: Make sure the business does not stop when one person is away
jobs.why: If only one person holds a login, a supplier contact or a key file, their holiday or exit can stop orders, ads or payments.

watch.metric: count of key systems, suppliers and files with only one person who can run them
watch.source: owner and backup list in the brand brain

drives.metric: days of work blocked by an absence per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 9 key systems have one person with access, including the 3PL portal and the bank. After: each has a named backup within 30 days.

jobs.job: Stop paying for software we do not use
jobs.why: Apps and tools pile up one small bill at a time. Many seats sit unused or overlap with another tool.

watch.metric: software spend as a share of revenue and count of tools or seats unused for 30 days, monthly
watch.source: card and expense feed, app admin panels

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 41 tools cost $6,300 a month and 9 are unused. After: 9 are cancelled and 4 downgraded, saving $1,700 a month.

jobs.job: Give every job and every number one owner
jobs.why: When 2 people half own something, it falls between them. When nobody owns it, it waits.

watch.metric: share of recurring decisions and key numbers with exactly 1 named owner
watch.source: owner list in the brand brain

drives.metric: tasks missed or late per month

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 14 of 30 recurring decisions have no clear owner, like reorders and promo approval. After: all 30 have 1 owner within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Keep supplier production on time and to spec
jobs.why: A late or faulty production run means stockouts, refunds or a rushed air freight bill. One tracker with one owner per step catches slips early.

watch.metric: share of purchase orders delivered by the promised date and passing quality checks, per order
watch.source: purchase order tracker in the brand brain, supplier emails

drives.metric: days out of stock on top products

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 of the last 5 orders arrived 2 to 4 weeks late with no early warning. After: each step has a date and owner and the next 4 orders land on time.

jobs.job: Plan warehouse and support capacity for peak season
jobs.why: Black Friday and holiday volume can break a 3PL and a support team that were fine all year. Capacity has to be agreed weeks ahead.

watch.metric: forecast peak daily orders against agreed 3PL and support capacity per day, checked 8 weeks before peak
watch.source: Shopify order history, 3PL capacity agreement, Gorgias staffing plan

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: last year's peak ran 5 days late on shipping. After: the 3PL agrees to 2,500 orders a day ahead of time and peak ships on time.

jobs.job: Remove access the day someone leaves
jobs.why: Ex-staff and old agencies with live access to the store, ads or bank are a theft and damage risk.

watch.metric: share of exits with all access removed the same day
watch.source: Shopify staff accounts, Meta Business Manager, Google, Klaviyo, bank user lists

drives.metric: active accounts held by people who left

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 2 past freelancers and 1 old agency still have admin access. After: all 3 are removed today and a same-day checklist runs on every exit.

jobs.job: Know if my agency earns its fee
jobs.why: Agencies report platform numbers that look good. The owner needs to see the profit the agency's channel brings after its fee.

watch.metric: contribution margin from the agency's channel after its fee, monthly
watch.source: Shopify orders, ad spend, agency invoices

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the agency reports 3.8x return on ad spend. After: channel margin after the $9,000 fee is $4,000 a month, so the fee moves to a share of margin.

jobs.job: Cut fulfilment cost per order
jobs.why: Pick, pack, postage and packaging add up to one of the biggest costs per order, and rates drift up every year.

watch.metric: fulfilment cost per order (pick, pack, packaging and postage), monthly
watch.source: 3PL invoices and shipping labels, Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: fulfilment costs $9.40 an order. After: 2 carriers and 1 new 3PL are quoted, and the cost falls to $8.10 within 90 days.

jobs.job: Log each big decision with the number it should move and a review date
jobs.why: Without a log, the team forgets why it chose something, repeats old debates and never checks if it worked.

watch.metric: share of big decisions logged with an owner, a target number and a review date
watch.source: decision log in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: no decisions are logged. After: 12 decisions a month are logged and 80% are reviewed on their date.

jobs.job: Catch software renewals before they auto-renew
jobs.why: Annual contracts renew quietly. Once the window closes, the brand pays another year for a tool it may have outgrown.

watch.metric: renewals in the next 60 days with a usage review done
watch.source: billing records and contracts in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 annual tools renew next month with no review. After: 1 is cancelled and 2 are cut to fewer seats, saving $7,000 a year.

jobs.job: Write down how each core job is done
jobs.why: If a task lives only in one head, nobody else can cover it and new hires take months to learn it.

watch.metric: share of core roles with a written how-to updated in the last 6 months
watch.source: how-to list in the brand brain

drives.metric: tasks missed when someone is away

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 4 of 11 core roles have a current written how-to. After: all 11 do within 2 months, starting with reorders and returns.

jobs.job: Keep the cost of each support ticket in check
jobs.why: Support cost rises with orders, but it should not rise faster. When it does, something upstream is broken.

watch.metric: support cost per ticket and tickets per 100 orders, monthly
watch.source: Gorgias or Zendesk, support payroll and vendor cost

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: cost per ticket rose from $4.10 to $5.30 in a quarter. After: top 3 ticket causes are fixed upstream and cost is back to $4.20.

jobs.job: Brief contractors properly: scope, rights and payment
jobs.why: Freelancers without a written scope, rights to their work and clear payment terms cause rework, disputes and lost files.

watch.metric: share of contractor engagements with signed scope, rights to the work and agreed payment terms
watch.source: contract list in the brand brain

drives.metric: contractor disputes or rework per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 5 of 9 active freelancers have no signed scope. After: all 9 sign a one-page brief within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Keep help answers current and reply quality high
jobs.why: Old answers in the help library send customers wrong info on returns or shipping, which brings more tickets and refunds.

watch.metric: quality score on a weekly sample of tickets and share of saved replies updated in the last 90 days
watch.source: Gorgias or Zendesk

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 40% of saved replies are over a year old and quality scores 72 out of 100. After: replies are refreshed and scores reach 88 within 6 weeks.

jobs.job: Act on what customers tell us
jobs.why: Complaints and requests reach support, reviews and surveys, but nobody owns turning them into fixes.

watch.metric: share of the top 10 customer complaints with an owner and a fix date, monthly
watch.source: Gorgias tags, reviews, survey answers

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: sizing and slow delivery lead complaints for 6 months with no owner. After: both have an owner and a fix date, and sizing tickets fall 30% in 2 months.

jobs.job: See when someone is overloaded before work drops
jobs.why: An overloaded person misses reorders, replies and launches. Seeing the load early lets the owner shift work or hire.

watch.metric: open tasks or tickets per person against their own normal level, weekly (proxy for workload)
watch.source: Gorgias assignments and the task list in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the operations lead holds 3 times their normal open tasks and 2 reorders slipped. After: 2 duties move to a freelancer and overdue tasks fall to 0.

jobs.job: Hire when a number says so, not when it feels busy
jobs.why: Hiring late burns out the team; hiring early burns cash. A written trigger, like tickets per agent or orders per operations person, sets the timing.

watch.metric: hiring trigger number against its threshold and weeks past the threshold with no opening
watch.source: Gorgias, Shopify orders, hiring triggers in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: support passed 90 tickets per agent a day 6 weeks ago and no hire is open. After: a part-time role opens this week.

jobs.job: Keep contracts and staff paperwork signed and current
jobs.why: Missing contracts or an unsigned handbook leave the brand exposed in a dispute or exit.

watch.metric: share of staff and contractors with a current signed contract and handbook
watch.source: staff records in the brand brain or HR tool

drives.metric: disputes with past staff per year

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 of 12 staff have not signed the current handbook. After: all 12 sign within 2 weeks.

jobs.job: Get new hires doing the job alone fast
jobs.why: A slow start costs salary with little output and pulls the founder back into training.

watch.metric: days until a new hire runs their core task alone (proxy: first solo run logged in the brand brain)
watch.source: task log in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: new hires take about 60 days to work alone. After: written how-tos and a week 1 walk through cut it to 25 days.
